title: Foreign Exchange Rates - H.10 - April 20, 2026
summary: The Federal Reserve released weekly H.10 foreign exchange rate data covering the period April 13-17, 2026, showing exchange rates for 20+ currencies against the US dollar alongside broad dollar indexes. The broad USD index closed at 118.0795 (Jan06=100) on April 17, down from 118.9916 on April 13. Euro traded at 1.1801 per USD on April 17; yen was 158.10 per USD; pound was 1.3556 per USD.
key_points: Release date: April 20, 2026, covering April 13-17 trading week
US Dollar Broad Index (Jan06=100): 118.0795 on April 17, down from 118.9916 on April 13 — 0.77% decline over the week
Euro (EMU members): 1.1710 to 1.1801 range across the week, closing stronger
Japanese Yen: ranged 158.10 to 159.74 per USD, ending at 158.10 (yen strengthened)
UK Pound: ranged 1.3459 to 1.3569, closing at 1.3556
Emerging Market Dollar Index (EME): closed at 127.6095, down from 128.4134 — 0.63% decline
Data excludes: no data available for certain dates (noted as 'ND = No data for this date')
why_it_matters: H.10 exchange rate data is the official US government source for currency valuation, used as reference by central banks, institutional investors, and corporations. Weekly movements in the broad dollar index signal aggregate USD strength or weakness against US trading partners. However, this source presents raw data without commentary or interpretation — no policy signals or macro narrative is provided.
